correctness.rationale: For an even selected set in a complete multipartite graph, a perfect matching exists exactly when no selected part has more than half of the selected vertices. Necessity is immediate from matching across parts; sufficiency is given by an explicit half-shift pairing of consecutive part-blocks. This balance condition also forces at least two selected parts, hence domination. Overload events for distinct parts are disjoint, giving the coefficient formula. Exact enumeration through order nine checks the characterization, coefficients, support, and quadratic coefficient.
